response.initial_request: I have received a message about a possible heating-system visit, but I do not have a confirmed appointment. Please check what has been arranged.

other_sections.Attachments: No attachments are available for this case.

events.body: Tenant reports that a caller identifying himself as a heating contractor asked her to leave the front-door key in the outside meter cabinet for a possible visit on Wednesday morning, May 14. She has no appointment window and has not agreed to a visit or key arrangement.
Opened maintenance enquiry NBL-029-01. Property record shows no active work order or confirmed appointment for the reported heating visit.
Tenant says the caller gave the name Bram Alder and called from 07700 900683. She confirmed the property when asked but did not provide an entry code or other access details.
Asked whether he had arranged heating work at the property, identified the contractor, or agreed a date or key arrangement.

Landlord says he asked someone to look into intermittent boiler pressure loss but has not fixed a date or discussed keys or access with the tenant. He cannot confirm the caller's identity from the name provided.

Tenant says she will be away during the proposed Wednesday morning period. Her 15-year-old son may return from school while she is out; she does not consider him an access contact and does not want him asked to let anyone in.
Forwards a message from Bram Alder saying he 'might call in Wednesday morning'. It contains no appointment window, work reference, business address, or confirmation that the tenant has agreed access.

Requested confirmation of his current business identity and contact details, the work he understands he has been asked to perform, and the proposed visit time. Asked whether he had requested that the tenant leave a key in the meter cabinet.

Says he understood Orren Vale wanted him to 'check the boiler' and that Wednesday morning might suit. Says the meter-cabinet key request was intended to avoid a wasted journey. His reply includes no work reference or business address.
Tenant says the meter cabinet is outside and shared with neighboring homes. She asks whether a visit has actually been arranged and says she has no appointment details.

Landlord says Bram Alder has previously done work for him at another property, but he has not checked the contractor's current business details or insurance. He wants the pressure issue investigated but has not specified a date.

Bram says Wednesday was not booked as a confirmed appointment and that he has not started travelling. He describes the task as an initial visual check and pressure reading, not a specified repair. He does not provide a business landline during the call.

Maintenance enquiry NBL-029-01 remains open. Correspondence logged: landlord email of 12 May at 10:11 and contractor call of 13 May at 08:03. Work-order appointment entry: EMPTY. External key-drop authorisation field: EMPTY.

Landlord authorizes a diagnostic visit by a suitably identified heating contractor to investigate intermittent pressure loss. He does not confirm that Bram Alder is currently engaged by Hearthline Boiler Service and has not agreed entry while the tenant is absent or an external key arrangement.

Tenant reports the heating is currently working, although boiler pressure has dropped intermittently during the past month. She could be home Saturday, May 17, between 10:00 and 12:00 if the visitor and purpose are confirmed in advance.
Bram says Saturday might be possible but he has not checked his schedule. He asks for the tenant's mobile number so he can coordinate directly. No visit time or company contact details are provided.

Tenancy record holds Elowen Vey's contact details. Consent field for disclosure to Bram Alder: EMPTY. Appointment correspondence logged: tenant message of 13 May at 11:41 and contractor email of 13 May at 12:26.

Tenant reports a message from the same number used by the caller: 'Still aiming for Saturday. If you're out, key in the meter cabinet would help.' The message gives no appointment window or business address.
Asked the landlord to clarify whether Bram Alder is the contractor he intends to engage and to confirm the access arrangements he is authorizing. No reply is yet recorded.
Message from 07700 900683: 'I can come Saturday sometime between 08:00 and 13:00. Can you confirm and leave the key in the meter cabinet if you won't be there?' The tenant has not replied.

args.subject: Heating visit at 62 Brindlewick Row, Vellumby, ZZ1 1ZZ - nothing confirmed yet
args.body:
Hello Elowen, to answer your question: no visit has been confirmed. Our records show no work order and no appointment (events 2, 13). The landlord has authorised a diagnostic visit for the intermittent boiler pressure loss, but only by a suitably identified heating contractor (event 14). We are still verifying the contractor, Bram Alder, who has given no company details or reference.

Please do not leave a key in the meter cabinet, and do not reply to the 08:00-13:00 Saturday message yet (event 20). We have not given your mobile number to anyone, and we will not without your consent. We will only confirm a visit once the contractor's identity and the purpose are verified. We will also check it fits your Saturday 17 May 10:00-12:00 availability (event 15). We will write to you as soon as we have confirmed details.

args.subject: Please confirm contractor and access - 62 Brindlewick Row, Vellumby, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body:
Hello Orren, following up on my email of 14 May (event 19), to which we have no reply yet. Before any visit goes ahead at 62 Brindlewick Row, Vellumby, ZZ1 1ZZ, please confirm:
1. Is Bram Alder (Hearthline Boiler Service) the contractor you want to engage for the boiler pressure check? He has given no company address, work reference or insurance details (events 9, 12, 16).
2. Please confirm that no key may be left in the shared outside meter cabinet and that entry is only with the tenant present. The tenant has not agreed to a key drop and is available on Saturday 17 May, 10:00-12:00 (events 15, 18).
Your 13 May email authorised a diagnostic visit by a suitably identified contractor (event 14). We will not confirm any appointment until we have your answer and the contractor's identity details.

args.subject: Verification needed before any visit - 62 Brindlewick Row, Vellumby, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body:
Hello Bram, there is no confirmed appointment at 62 Brindlewick Row, Vellumby, ZZ1 1ZZ, and you are not yet instructed. Please do not ask the tenant to leave a key in the meter cabinet. The cabinet is shared and no key drop is authorised. Please send:
1. Your business name, business address and a landline or office contact number.
2. Proof of insurance.
3. The scope of the visit (initial visual check and pressure reading, as you described on 13 May).
4. A specific arrival window. The tenant is only available on Saturday 17 May, 10:00-12:00, and will be present. Your 08:00-13:00 proposal does not match this.
We will not pass on the tenant's phone number without her consent. Once we have this and the landlord's confirmation, we will confirm any appointment in writing.

args.summary: No visit is confirmed. The landlord authorised a diagnostic visit only by a suitably identified contractor. Bram Alder's identity is unverified and he keeps asking for a key left in a shared cabinet. I told the tenant nothing is confirmed and not to leave a key. I chased the landlord for a contractor and access confirmation. I asked the contractor for identity, insurance, scope and a window that fits the tenant's availability.
args.answer_to_question: No visit has been confirmed. There is no work order or appointment (events 2, 13). Bram's Wednesday visit was never booked (event 12). His Saturday 08:00-13:00 proposal (event 20) is unconfirmed and the tenant has not agreed to it.
facts: No work order or appointment on record (events 2, 13)
Landlord asked someone to look at boiler pressure loss but fixed no date or access (event 5)
Landlord authorised a diagnostic visit only by a suitably identified contractor, and has not agreed a key drop or entry while the tenant is out (event 14)
Contractor gave no work reference, business address or company contact (events 9, 12, 16)
Tenant is free Saturday 17 May 10:00-12:00 if visitor and purpose are confirmed, and does not want her son used as an access contact (events 6, 15)
Contractor proposed 08:00-13:00 and a key in the shared meter cabinet (events 18, 20)
No tenant consent to share her number (event 17)
Landlord has not replied to the 14 May clarification request (event 19)
conflicts: The contractor says the landlord asked him to check the boiler (event 9). The landlord cannot confirm his identity or current engagement (events 5, 14).
The contractor's 08:00-13:00 Saturday window does not match the tenant's 10:00-12:00 availability (events 15, 20).
missing: Landlord confirmation that Bram Alder / Hearthline is the intended contractor
Contractor's verified business and insurance details
A confirmed appointment window agreed with the tenant
Tenant consent before sharing her phone number
options_rejected: Instructing or booking the contractor: identity unverified and access not agreed
Escalating now: the landlord's reply to a single outstanding question can settle the contractor identity
Waiting without sending anything: the tenant needs a clear answer and the key-drop risk needs stopping
args.uncertainty: Whether the contractor is genuine is unknown. If the landlord and contractor do not answer, or the contractor keeps pushing the key drop, this should go to the property manager as a possible security risk.
